name: Black Basta
description: Black Basta was a top-tier Russian-speaking ransomware-as-a-service operation that splintered from Conti in early 2022 and went on to extort hundreds of organizations, primarily via QakBot and Brute Ratel-delivered initial access. The operation effectively collapsed in February 2025 after an internal chat-log leak ('BlackBastaGPT') exposed its operators, victim negotiations, and infrastructure, combined with the prior law-enforcement takedown of the QakBot botnet (Operation Duck Hunt). Its data-leak site went dark by the end of February 2025 and no new Black Basta-branded encryptions have been confirmed since. In January 2026, German and Ukrainian law enforcement raided the homes of alleged 'hash cracker' affiliates and publicly identified group leader Oleg Evgenievich Nefedov ('GG'), adding him to the EU Most Wanted list and an INTERPOL Red Notice. Researchers assess that surviving members and affiliates dispersed into other RaaS brands â€” including CACTUS, SafePay, and the newer DevMan operation built on leaked Conti/Black Basta and DragonForce code â€” meaning the Black Basta brand itself remains dormant even as its TTPs and personnel persist under other names.

ttps.notes: Historically delivered via QakBot email campaigns prior to the botnet's 2023 takedown
Microsoft Teams helpdesk impersonation and email-bombing used to gain initial foothold (overlap with Storm-1811/UNC6692-style activity)
Abused legitimate remote management tools (e.g., Quick Assist, AnyDesk) for hands-on-keyboard access after social engineering
ChaCha20-based Black Basta encryptor with double-extortion leak site
Used Rclone to exfiltrate data to cloud storage prior to encryption
Brute Ratel and Cobalt Strike used for credential theft and lateral movement
Deleted volume shadow copies and disabled recovery options prior to encryption

notable_techniques: Operation effectively ended after the 2025 'BlackBastaGPT' internal chat-log leak exposed operator identities, infrastructure, and victim negotiations
Leak site went dark by end of February 2025 with no confirmed new encryptions under the Black Basta brand since
Group leader 'GG' (Oleg Nefedov) publicly identified and added to EU Most Wanted / INTERPOL Red Notice in January 2026
January 2026 raids targeted affiliate 'hash crackers' specializing in cracking passwords from compromised systems
Members and tooling assessed to have dispersed into CACTUS, SafePay, and the emerging DevMan ransomware brand
Heavy reliance on Microsoft Teams-based helpdesk impersonation for initial access, a TTP later adopted widely by other crews
detection_opportunities: Legacy IOC matching against historical Black Basta/QakBot infrastructure for retrospective hunting
Detection rules tuned for successor brands (CACTUS, SafePay, DevMan) given personnel and tooling overlap
Monitoring for Microsoft Teams external-access helpdesk impersonation patterns inherited by successor groups
Rclone execution and unusual outbound traffic to cloud storage providers preceding mass file modification
Volume shadow copy deletion (vssadmin/wmic) combined with rapid file encryption activity
Brute Ratel C4 and Cobalt Strike beacon signatures on endpoint and network telemetry
response_playbook: Run retrospective hunts against legacy Black Basta/QakBot IOCs even though the brand is largely defunct.
Tune detections for successor brands (CACTUS, SafePay, DevMan) given documented personnel and tooling overlap.
Monitor for Microsoft Teams external-access helpdesk impersonation â€” a TTP this group pioneered that successors have inherited.
Hunt for Rclone execution and unusual outbound traffic to cloud storage preceding mass file modification.
